audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven phases[N].side disagree with content win[N]. Full layer reads Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Vex/Skill/Skill; content reads Hwei/Hwei/Hwei/Skill/Skill/Hwei/Hwei.
audit.why: packet.levelChart matches the content layer exactly; win rate 54.52% over 1506 games.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 2, 5 and 6 moved to Hwei and row 4 to Skill as one atomic group, with phases[4].why rewritten so the level 6 row argues the even verdict instead of a Hwei all-in.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text calls both ultimates "fear/root tools" and spikes[3].text calls hers "R-Shadow Surge fear".
audit.why: Shadow Surge is 140/120/100s at 2000/2500/3000 range: a missile that marks a champion, recast to dash to them and deal damage. The fear is Doom 'n Gloom, her passive. Her ultimate applies no fear at all.
audit.corrected: Level 6 and late spikes re-keyed to the mark-and-dash at 2000 range, with the fear attributed to the passive.
sources: enemyKit R text, cd and range

audit.whatIsWrong: The page names the fear "Personal Space (Fear)" in focus.text, winCon, enemyWin, loading, breakdown.cooldowns and five report entries. wants.foe[0] credits Personal Space with true damage. wants.you[1] tells you to avoid dashing near her. wants.you[2] puts the fear on Hwei's W. spikes[0], whys[1], whys[5], spikes[3] and late all describe Mistral Bolt or her kit as short-range.
audit.why: Personal Space (W) is a 475-range shield that damages nearby enemies — no fear, no true damage anywhere in her kit. The fear is Doom 'n Gloom (P), which empowers her next basic ability. Mistral Bolt (Q) is 1200 range and accelerates mid-flight, which is not short. Hwei's fear lives in the E form, not W. Most importantly: Doom 'n Gloom's dash-mark and dash-interrupt are dead weight in this matchup, because Hwei has no dash on any ability — she cannot mark you and cannot shorten her empowered cooldown off you, so every fear she gets she has to wait out in full.
audit.corrected: Fear moved to the passive throughout, the true-damage claim deleted, Q stated at its real 1200 range, and the no-dash consequence written in as the reason the lane is winnable.
sources: ownerKit — no dash on any ability

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns has no digit (lintFindings) and dosFull[2].d offers a "fifteen-second invitation".
audit.why: Personal Space is 16s at rank 1 falling to 12s, Looming Darkness is a flat 12s, Mistral Bolt 8s falling to 4s, Shadow Surge 140s at rank 1. Doom 'n Gloom's recharge is not a number Riot's text gives, so I stated the behaviour instead.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written in; the fifteen-second claim removed rather than replaced with a guess.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing told the reader her shield eats the burst they are setting up.
audit.why: Personal Space grants a shield on a 16-second rank-1 cooldown, which absorbs the signature detonation if it goes up first.
audit.corrected: Added to dosFull[1].d and breakdown.mid: force the shield out with one paint, then land the two-spell mark.

notes: THE FEAR WAS ON THE WRONG ABILITY EVERYWHERE. 'Personal Space (Fear)' appeared in focus.text, loading, winCon, enemyWin, breakdown.cooldowns and four report entries. Personal Space (W) is a 475-range shield that damages nearby enemies and fears nothing; the fear is Doom 'n Gloom, her passive, which empowers her next basic ability. wants.foe[0] also invented true damage on it — nothing in Vex's kit deals true damage. THE INTERACTION NOBODY WROTE DOWN: Doom 'n Gloom's whole punish mechanic is dash-based — it interrupts dashes and marks nearby enemies who dash, and consuming that mark is what shortens her empowered cooldown. Hwei has no dash on any ability, so in this specific matchup that half of her passive is inert and she can never accelerate her fear off you. wants.you[1] previously told the reader to 'avoid dashing near her', advice Hwei physically cannot follow. RANGE: four fields called Mistral Bolt or her kit short-range; Q is 1200 and accelerates mid-flight. CHART: six sides realigned to the packet-backed content layer as one atomic group, with phases[4].why rewritten to match its new Skill verdict; no paired win[N] edits because win[N] already holds the correct token. RATINGS left untouched. LEFT ALONE: content.mid and whys[3] describe both ultimates as crowd control deciding who lands first. Shadow Surge marks and dashes but Riot's text gives it no crowd control, so the framing is loose — I could not tell whether the mark itself is intended as the 'CC' and did not want to rewrite a whole paragraph on a guess.
